summary: shinko is meant to become a resource, perhaps a flavour of delta: a realtime shared tree with formulas
detail: Peter, 3 Oct: shinko is just another resource, a realtime shared tree, and it should evolve into one, perhaps as a flavour of delta. It is work in progress, so the evolve skill only names it and has no section for it yet. Things found while looking: shinko is a private repo and not on npm ("private": true), so `bun add github:blueshed/shinko` answers 404 without a token. It serves a person over a Bun WebSocket (`serve`, with `foreign` and `sending`), and a page uses `connect` from `shinko/client`; `examples/socket.ts` and `examples/echo` are the smallest hosts. Two questions for when it is a resource: its socket next to the app's `/ws` (Bun.serve has one websocket handler, so the two need telling apart by ws.data, or one socket carries both), and installing it.

summary: duckdown's bun-create postinstall is "bun run create/setup.ts", which bun create runs with a second `bun run` in front: nothing happens
detail: Found building paintbrush's create script. bun create prefixes every postinstall entry with `bun run`, so an entry that starts with `bun run` does nothing, silently. Checked on Bun 1.4.2 by running duckdown's own create from a local copy (BUN_CREATE_DIR): the created site kept the template's todo.jsonl and create/, and had no site/. The entry that works is create/setup.ts. The GitHub path was not run, but Bun's docs say it shares the steps. duckdown's ledger and README are the home for this; it is noted here so the finding is not lost.
note: 2026-10-02: found; not yet told to duckdown. Open, for Peter.

summary: The migrations step and the build step do not go together: a build looks for the migrations in dist/migrations
detail: migrations.md loads a resource's migrations with fromFolder(`${import.meta.dir}/migrations`). build.md bundles src/main.ts into dist/, and in a bundle import.meta.dir is dist/ (checked on Bun 1.4.3 with a two-file build), so a built app would look for dist/migrations, which the build does not make, and fail at start-up. test:evolve applies each step on its own after the steps it builds on, so it never builds an app with migrations. Ways out: the build copies each resource's migrations/ beside main.js, or a resource lists its migrations by import, which bundles them. Not decided, so the skill says nothing of it yet.
note: 2026-10-15: found writing the migrations step (delta 0.16.0); open.

summary: The Postgres step does not take delta 0.14.0's migrate or createDocListener's schema
detail: delta 0.14.0 gives Postgres and PGlite the same migrate as SQLite (await migrate(pool, list, { app, schema }), then applyFramework and applySql(generateSql(...))), and createDocListener a schema, so a process writes and sees by its own schema when two versions share a database. postgres.md replaces orderDocs whole, so the SQLite migrations step does not carry into it. Left as it is at the session's brief: the Postgres split (~/Workshop/docs/postgres-split-plan.md) moves this step to dzql, and it takes both there.
note: 2026-10-15: found aligning with delta 0.16.0; open until the step points at dzql.

summary: A browser test can time out on CI's Chrome, and every page test after it fails on a pending navigation
detail: On PR #7 (2026-10-15) the first page test timed out at 30 s waiting for the page on the runner's Chrome, and the message tests after it failed with 'a navigation is already pending'. Re-run unchanged, all passed. Two things: the first page's wait could allow for a slow browser start on CI, and a test that times out should leave the WebView ready for the next (navigate away or recreate it), so one slow start does not fail the file.
note: 2026-10-15: seen once, on the delta 1.0 PR; passed on re-run. 2026-10-15: fixed in tests/browser.ts: browser() makes the first navigation in its own beforeAll (2 min), and navigations wait for the last to settle; proven both ways with a scratch test that holds a page past a test's time.
